findings.title: Public select/future docs still describe `error.Closed` as terminal-only, but this push makes it ambiguous.
findings.detail: The future-protocol contract says a queue arm reports readiness only for a takeable completion or a drained queue, and `getResult` then reports `error.Closed` for that drained state. But this commit explicitly allows `getResult` to return `error.Closed` on stale wakes while the queue is still open/not drained (lines 309-321), requiring a follow-up `isDrained()` check. Consumers following the unchanged contract comment can still treat `error.Closed` as terminal and stop driving too early (including closed-but-not-drained scenarios), leaking in-flight completions. Update the public contract comments/examples to require `isDrained()` disambiguation on `error.Closed` from select.

findings.title: No regression test exercises the new `isDrained()` disambiguation path.
findings.detail: This push introduces `isDrained()` as the required guard after `error.Closed` from queue futures, but the test suite never asserts that driver behavior. Existing tests cover close/drain behavior and select outcomes, yet none verifies the new contract: on `error.Closed`, `isDrained()==false` must keep driving and `isDrained()==true` is the only stop condition. Without a dedicated test, this API-level fix can regress silently.
